visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A man with short graying hair and glasses wearing a black button-up shirt stands centrally against a night cityscape backdrop with a banner at the top displaying "AI Forum 2025". He is looking directly at the camera with a neutral expression. (2) Close-up shot of a chimpanzee's head and face against a lush green forest background; the chimpanzee has its mouth wide open in a vocalization posture. (3) The scene returns to the man in the black shirt speaking; he begins to move his hands expressively as he talks, maintaining his position in front of the illuminated city skyline. (4) A digital screen capture displays a scientific paper titled "Chimpanzee drumming shows rhythmicity and subspecies variation" with multiple authors and highlights listed below the title. (5) Back to the man in the black shirt who is now gesturing with both hands while speaking; the background remains the same nighttime urban view with red and yellow lights. (6) A handheld video clip shows a chimpanzee in a dark forest environment, physically striking a large, horizontal tree root with its hands to create a rhythmic vibration. (7) A brief close-up of the chimpanzee's face again, showing its facial features and dark fur clearly in natural daylight. (8) The man continues his presentation, occasionally shrugging or pointing to emphasize his points while a subtitle overlay appears at the bottom of the frame. (9) An animated clip features two characters in a room with posters, playing a drum set and a guitar; the colors are vibrant and the style is modern 2D animation. (10) The man concludes by pointing downwards toward the bottom of the screen where variety captions and social media prompts are visible.
visual_base.text_narrative_log: (1) [Logo]: 泛科學 NEWS. [Slogan]: AI Forum 2025 人工智慧論壇. [Subtitle]: 猩猩. (2) [Slogan]: 什麼？黑猩猩也有節奏感？ [Subtitle]: 一起. (3) [Subtitle]: 強大. (4) [Subtitle]: 最新研究發現. (5) [Subtitle]: 黑猩猩竟然會打鼓. (6) [Subtitle]: 而且還有自己的演奏風格. (7) [Subtitle]: 英國聖安德魯斯大學的科學家. (8) [Subtitle]: 在烏干達森林裡. (9) [Subtitle]: 觀察了野生黑猩猩敲擊樹根的行為. (10) [Subtitle]: 發現牠們不是隨便亂敲. (11) [Subtitle]: 反而好像還蠻在意節奏感的. (12) [Subtitle]: 更神奇的是不同地區的黑猩猩. (13) [Subtitle]: 演奏風格還不一樣. (14) [Subtitle]: 就跟粽子有分南部粽跟北部粽一樣. (15) [Subtitle]: 研究團隊分析11個黑猩猩族群的. [Variety]: 371段打鼓錄音. (16) [Subtitle]: 發現西非的黑猩猩敲擊節奏均勻. (17) [Subtitle]: 像人類的四四拍. (18) [Subtitle]: 一下一下很穩. (19) [Subtitle]: 而東非的黑猩猩則喜歡一長一短交替的拍子. (20) [Subtitle]: 有點像搖滾樂的切分音. (21) [Subtitle]: 之外牠們敲擊樹根的聲音. (22) [Subtitle]: 有些還可以傳超過一公里. (23) [Subtitle]: 而且牠們還會搭配經典的呼喊叫聲. (24) [Subtitle]: 像這樣. (25) [Subtitle]: 這表示黑猩猩可能通過不同的敲打節奏. (26) [Subtitle]: 跟叫聲來跟同伴進行溝通. (27) [Subtitle]: 欸我是說可能. (28) [Subtitle]: 這部分還沒證實. (29) [Subtitle]: 這發現也讓科學家推測. (30) [Subtitle]: 節奏感這種能力. (31) [Subtitle]: 或許是來自我們跟黑猩猩的共同祖先. (32) [Subtitle]: 哇真是太棒了. (33) [Subtitle]: 我們可以請黑猩猩一起來. (34) [Subtitle]: 就愛韓德爾. (35) [Subtitle]: 想了解更多科學新聞嗎？快點這裡. [Variety]: 快留言許願 下週《泛科NEWS》就來發!.
